The Permanent Wave Precinct

On the first day of absentee voting at a nursing-home salon, a hairdresser, a county election worker, and a retired civics teacher try to keep democracy dry, private, and out of the shampoo bowl. Then an unopened ballot addressed to a dead woman turns a procedural morning into a family reckoning.

A line to remember: “The voter should not be displayed like ham.”

3,625 words · 23 min listen
